purpose: Candidate attention kernel implementations, collected to serve as A-tier answers, B-tier expert dispatch bases, or expert references. These are implementations, not primitive operators.
collection_method: upstream documentation and repository metadata read directly; every claim below carries the page it came from so it can be re-checked without trusting this file
headline: The fused attention path is an S5000 story. MATE requires S5000, MT-flashMLA targets compute capability 3.1, and MUTLASS's MP31 work is mp_31 too. mp_31 is S5000; the machine available here is S4000 at mp_22. So the fused-library route the B tier is built around does not exist on the target currently in hand, and the S4000 profile of torch SDPA (five kernels, two assembly SGEMMs plus a softmax) is consistent with a decomposition rather than a fused kernel.

candidates.name: MATE FMHA forward (mate.mha_interface, and the flash_attn_3 compatibility wrapper)

upstream.note: MATE keeps its own version; installing a wrapper (flash_attn_3, flash_mla, sageattention, fmha_sm100, flashinfer-python, flash_kda, deep-gemm) pulls the matching mate package in automatically. Wrapper releases carry the PEP 440 local suffix +musa.

limits.alignment_fp16_bf16_without_qv: Q/K and V head dim must be divisible by 2
limits.alignment_with_qv: divisible by 8, and V head dim <= 512
limits.layout: BSHD; the documented tensor shapes are (batch, seqlen, nheads, headdim)

candidates.why_it_matters: This is the only candidate that provides a genuine fused forward attention path, and its argument list maps onto the B-tier SDPA task contract almost field for field: window_size (-1, -1) for unbounded, causal, softmax_scale, return_softmax_lse, pack_gqa. It is also BSHD-native while the B-tier task is BHSD, so a MATE-based dispatch has to transpose, which is itself a dispatch-cost question worth grading.

candidates.name: MT-flashMLA

limits.scope: decoding only, not a general forward attention kernel

candidates.why_it_matters: Narrower than MATE and superseded by it for general forward attention, but it is a second, independent mp_31 attention implementation. Useful as a cross-check that a MATE result is not an artifact of one kernel family. Not usable for any entry in the attention set, all of which are forward.

candidates.name: MUTLASS experimental/fmha (source-level)

upstream.note: Fork of NVIDIA/cutlass. MUTLASS 0.3.0 added a warp-specialized GEMM mainloop targeting the MP31 architecture.

requirements.note: source only; no documented wheel-level entry point

limits.usability: individual .mu files do not compile standalone; they depend on sibling headers, build configuration and a matching MUSA SDK

candidates.why_it_matters: This is the kind of source a maintainer reads when writing the expert dispatch or an A-tier kernel, not something to call at runtime. It is the honest answer to 'where does the expert knowledge come from' for mp_31.

candidates.name: torch_musa SDPA and the muDNN SDP integration

requirements.gpu: not documented as arch-limited in the sources consulted
requirements.note: the only candidate that plausibly covers mp_22 as well as mp_31

features.reached_via: the framework op, so the submission cannot tell which kernel answered

limits.open_question: whether the fused muDNN SDP path is selected on mp_22 at all, and for which shapes

candidates.why_it_matters: This is the route the existing B-tier SDPA task assumes for its fused_library path. The S4000 profile of problem 97 shows five device kernels, two assembly SGEMMs plus a softmax, which is a decomposition rather than a fused kernel. That is one shape at one dtype and does not settle whether the fused path exists on mp_22; it does mean the fused route must be probed per configuration rather than assumed. Resolving this is the first thing probe_sdpa.py should do on the real machine.
evidence: docs/musa/source_inventory.md (problem 97 row, and the attention source paths)

candidates.name: The hand-written MUSA attention kernels already in this repository

designs: flash-tile band with shared K/V streaming (43/44/50)
two-stage register-tiled SGEMM plus global row softmax (31/97)
one CTA per (window, head) whole-window staging (30)

limits.warp_size_sensitivity: tuned on mp_22 at 128-thread warps with the optimum at 1024 threads per CTA; not transferable to mp_31 at 32-thread warps without re-measuring
limits.shared_memory: launch configurations are valid only for the head_dim they were measured on

candidates.why_it_matters: These are the only attention kernels in hand that actually run on the machine available. They are A-tier answers, and they are also the naive-side data the B-tier admission gate needs. They are not candidates for the S5000 fused path.

candidates.name: TileLang MUSA legacy snapshot

requirements.note: snapshot not present locally; see the dangling references in the attention set

limits.status: deprecated upstream; the revision record calls it the final snapshot

candidates.why_it_matters: Recorded because the project's own source record lists it as an S4000/S5000 kernel reference candidate. Nothing can be said about its actual coverage from here: the snapshot is not in the repository and the revision is deprecated. Treat the claim in the source record as unverified until someone looks at the tree.

gaps: No candidate provides a fused forward attention path on mp_22. If the B-tier attention task is to be graded on S4000, either a fused path must be established there (probe first) or the task's library_policy must be rewritten so that fused_library is not the expected path.
Nothing here has been executed. Every dtypes, limits and alignment field above is transcribed from upstream documentation, not measured on hardware.
MT-flashMLA and MUTLASS fmha are mp_31 decode/source-level artifacts; the attention set is entirely forward attention, so neither maps onto a current entry.
